summary: Established a persistent AIDE integrity baseline for /etc on node1. The final database contains 1,900 entries, detects changes, reports clean after restoration, and remains valid after reboot. Run future checks with: sudo aide --config /etc/aide/etc-baseline.conf --check
actions_performed: Created /etc/aide/etc-baseline.conf scoped to /etc with metadata, ACL, extended-attribute, SHA-256, and SHA-512 checks.
Created the protected baseline database at /var/lib/aide/etc-baseline.db.gz.
Verified detection using a temporary /etc marker, then removed it and rebuilt a clean authoritative baseline.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed from 0256e3f5-9f2d-48f3-b55b-12f9f4d599ab to 80a5dd10-7911-4915-8227-1c031182384e.
Confirmed the system, AIDE installation, baseline database, checksum, and clean 1,900-entry comparison recovered after reboot.

evidence.summary: Shows the /etc-only rule, final database initialization, database checksum, 1,900 tracked entries, and a clean AIDE result.
A reversible test was reported as the exact added path /etc/.aide-integrity-test with nonzero status; the final restored baseline subsequently reported no differences.
Captures the healthy pre-restart state and old boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered running system with the same baseline SHA-256 and a clean AIDE check.
